title: Fair-share surge pools, temporary boosts, and post-burst smoothing for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated plans are experiencing variable costs and unfair throughput during short bursts. Current surge behavior grants temporary capacity on a first-come-first-served basis and bills overage at a flat rate. This causes noisy neighbor situations where a single tenant can consume most of the surge pool, and customers receive surprise overage charges that don't reflect effective throughput guarantees.

Goal: Implement a fair-share surge allocation algorithm, introduce temporary boost tokens with TTL and soft-reservation semantics, and add a post-burst smoothing window for billing to reduce cost surprises. Provide Console visibility (per-tenant surge usage, earned smoothing credits) and clear billing reconciliation rules.

Scope: Backend allocation logic, metering changes, billing reconciliation rules, API flags for boosting behavior, and console UI counters. Does not include changes to Dedicated SLA language or legal billing terms (PM to coordinate).

Success metrics: 1) Reduction in single-tenant surge monopolization by >= 80% on high contention pools (observed in staging). 2) Decrease in number of "unexpected overage" support tickets by 50% in first month after rollout. 3) Accurate billing reconciliation within 24 hours after burst window ends.
acceptance_criteria: Fair-share allocator enforces per-customer weight caps and does not allow any single tenant to exceed 40% of a surge pool over any 5-minute window in staging tests.
Temporary boost tokens are issued with TTL (default 10m) and an optional priority tag; tokens are revokable and visible in tenant usage logs.
Billing pipeline implements a post-burst smoothing window (default 2 hours) that averages burst consumption before final overage invoice is generated.
Console shows a per-tenant "surge credit" balance, recent boost events, and a projected overage estimate accounting for smoothing rules.
E2E tests cover allocator fairness, token issuance/expiration, reconciliation correctness, and metrics emitted to observability stack.
Backwards-compatible API: existing Dedicated customers keep prior behavior until opt-in flag is set; opt-in can be toggled in Console and via API.
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Raman: Ticket created after customer incident where XCorp consumed 78% of a surge pool and triggered high overage for neighbors. Linked incident notes and raw trace. Filed as P1 due to billing exposure.

2025-02-14 Luca Martinez: Spike allocator prototype pushed to feature branch (github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-serving/pull/1283). Prototype implements token buckets + weighted round-robin for surge grants. Needs performance review on 8xA10G cluster.

2025-02-18 Priya Nair (PM): Design doc uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Surge+FairShare+Design. PM note: legal to review billing language before GA; will coordinate with billing team.
2025-02-21 Eng review: Performance concern: RR allocator adds contention when pool size < 10. Luca to add fast-path for small pools that uses deterministic cap-based allocation.
2025-02-25 Analytics spike: simulated fair-share reduced max tenant share from 78% to 31% in 1,000 synthetic tests (see dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/alerts/surge-fairshare).

2025-02-28 Design feedback from UX (Marta Ortiz): Console mockups ok but request clearer terminology — use 'boost tokens' instead of 'ephemeral credits'. Will update mockups and include CTA to opt-in/out.

2025-03-03 Billing: Prototype smoothing logic added to billing-reconciler (github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/402). Note: reconciliation currently runs hourly; we need final decision on 2-hour smoothing window to avoid double-billing edge cases.
2025-03-05 Luca Martinez: Updated implementation plan attached. Integration testing scheduled for 2025-03-10 in staging cluster. Request code review from infra-team and billing team.
notes: Implementation trade-offs: strict caps guarantee fairness but may underutilize capacity when many low-traffic tenants exist. We expose an opt-in 'aggressive boost' for tenants that want best-effort higher burst at risk of increased overage.

Billing reconciliation: smoothing window chosen as 2 hours by default after consult with PM and billing. Shorter window (30m) caused more invoices with micro-overages; longer window (24h) delayed billing complaints and complicates refunds.
Telemetry: emit tenant-level surge_grant, token_issue, token_expire, and post_burst_adjustment events with tenant_id and weight for auditability.
Rollout plan: feature-flag all changes. Stage rollout in a subset of Dedicated pools (low risk customers) for 2 weeks, measure fairness and billing churn, then expand.
Follow-ups: PM to propose customer communication copy; Support to prepare KB article explaining smoothing and boost tokens.
